body_json.answer:
**Assessment:** rejected.

The new post poses a general question about whether police sometimes kill innocent Black people without consequence, a theme echoed in several retrieved posts. [T4-002635](#T4-002635) asserts "Another cop. Another black man. Another killing of innocent person," and [T4-003024](#T4-003024) asks why a Black person "gunned down by police" is "not criminal," sharing the new post's framing of lethal force against Black people as unjust. [T4-009282](#T4-009282) directly matches the "without consequence" element, claiming a "Cop who killed unarmed black man still isn't punished," while [T4-009367](#T4-009367) similarly laments that police crimes go unpunished ("Yet there's no justice"). The key difference is that the new post is phrased as an open question rather than an assertion, whereas the retrieved posts state these as claims or reporting; [T4-003184](#T4-003184) is only weakly related, questioning why Black people should trust police without addressing lethal force or accountability specifically.
